subject: lib/elf/elf_parse.c
text: This unit is shared by the kernel loader and userspace apps, which is why it lives in lib/ and not under kernel/ or sdk/. The constraint that forced the neutral location: tools/dbt/builder.py only auto-adds a source's *sibling* include/ to -I, so a header left in kernel/duneos_loader/include would be unreachable from an app build — elf.h and loader_limits.h had to move with it or the launcher does not link. Anything added here must stay C17 + libc with injected I/O: no ESP-IDF, no FreeRTOS, no kernel headers, or every .dap that pulls it breaks. See ADR 043. Apps reference it as $ROOT/lib/elf/elf_parse.c; the $ROOT/ prefix is bounded against traversal in builder.py's _resolve_under().

subject: sdk/app/libappmeta.c
text: appmeta_read() allocates e_shnum*40 for the section header table in one block, where the pre-DUP-01 reader streamed 16 headers at a time. With DUNEOS_LOADER_MAX_SECTIONS at 1024 the worst case is ~40 KiB against the launcher's 8192-byte pool, so an app past roughly 200 sections would fail with -ENOMEM and vanish from the launcher grid with no diagnostic (launcher.c ignores the appmeta_read error). Not live: measured max e_shnum across all 60 built app.elf is 18, and ADR 022 dropped -ffunction-sections/-fdata-sections which is what keeps it there. If that CFLAGS decision is ever reverted, this becomes reachable — check it before raising section granularity. Measured peak transient heap today is 864 B because the image is closed before the manifest malloc.
